title: Local setup and licenses
lead: Try the basic Web controls on localhost. Native apps, custom Web hosts, and Analytics require the appropriate license settings.

rows: Node.js / pnpm
24.19.0 / 10.33.0. Use the versions pinned by the repository.
Web Player / UI
Bitmovin Player 8.281.0 / Player UI 4.23.0, pinned to exact versions.
Browser
A browser that can play HLS or DASH. Codec support, external playback, and low-latency support depend on the environment.
Network
Dependency downloads, license authentication, and external reference streams require connectivity. Running locally does not by itself provide fully offline playback.

blocks.title: Clone and start for the first time
blocks.text:
git clone https://github.com/kazuhide/player-lab.git
cd player-lab
corepack enable
corepack prepare pnpm@10.33.0 --activate
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm --filter @showcase/web dev

Open the URL shown in the startup message using the hostname localhost. The Web SDK can run on this hostname without a Player key. LAN IP addresses, custom hostnames, GitHub Pages, and native apps require an appropriate license.

The normal development mode does not automatically use the same 60-second media as the public Pages build. Basic HLS uses Tears of Steel, DASH uses a public Big Buck Bunny stream, and live playback uses external reference streams. Some additional audio, subtitle, and image preview options remain unavailable until their media URLs are configured.
Create local settings only when needed

blocks.title: Run from the repository root
blocks.text:
cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env locally, then synchronize native settings.
bash scripts/sync-env.sh

Edit .env in your own editor. Normal local settings take precedence in this order: shell environment variables, the root .env file, then the public config/encoding.conf file. Explicit Web-specific VITE_* settings take priority. Restart the development server after changing settings. For native apps, synchronize the settings and rebuild.

rows: BITMOVIN_PLAYER_LICENSE_KEY
Client license for the Player. Allow the domains or application identifiers where it will run.
BITMOVIN_ANALYTICS_LICENSE_KEY
Optional client license for collecting playback events. Leave it empty to disable collection.
BITMOVIN_ANALYTICS_API_KEY
Optional server credential for local aggregate queries. Do not pass it to the browser.
BITMOVIN_API_KEY
Server or command-line credential for account API operations. The local Analytics proxy also accepts it as a fallback. Keep it out of client code.

blocks.title: Keep client licenses separate from account API keys
blocks.text: Player and Analytics licenses are delivered to clients. Manage their allowed domains and application identifiers. Keep account API keys on the server; do not place them in VITE_*, HTML, or client code. Use dedicated client licenses for a public demo.

rows: Web
Vite reads the root .env file. Additional media URLs can be configured in apps/web/.env.
iOS / tvOS
sync-env.sh writes Local.xcconfig. Generate the project with XcodeGen after the first synchronization.
Android
sync-env.sh writes local.properties. Explicit Gradle properties are also supported.
React Native
Move the generated EXPO_PUBLIC_* settings into the Expo project where you integrate the sample.
Vega OS
Set globalThis in the Kepler entry point. See the integration chapter for details.

blocks.text: For a fork or another deployment, configure the two public client licenses below as GitHub Repository variables and enable the included Pages workflow. Local .env files and inherited VITE_* values do not replace this configuration. CI builds and tests the artifact before Pages publishes it.

rows: PLAYER_LAB_PUBLIC_PLAYER_LICENSE_KEY
Dedicated Player license that allows the public host.
PLAYER_LAB_PUBLIC_ANALYTICS_LICENSE_KEY
Dedicated Analytics license that allows the public host.

blocks.text: The current public host is kazuhide.github.io. For another host, allow that hostname and check the paths, Pages settings, and applicable terms. These values are expected to be included in the distributed JavaScript. The current Pages workflow only deploys artifacts configured with both public client licenses. An account API key is not required.
